title: 8 Choo Young-woo K-dramas to revisit after "Between Steps" - Hashtag Legend Hong Kong
text:
8 Choo Young-woo K-dramas to revisit after "Between Steps" | #legend Culture Watches & Jewellery Fashion Lifestyle Beauty #legend100 #legend signature Culture Film & Series Music Art & Design Watches & Jewellery Fashion Lifestyle Dining Travel & Stays Tech & Gadgets Motors Wellness Beauty #legend100 #legend signature Hong Kong Subscribe culture entertainment film & series 8 Choo Young-woo K-dramas to revisit after "Between Steps"
 By Tom Kao November 19, 2026 Still thinking about Choo Young-woo and Kim So-hyun's romance in "Between Steps"? The slow-burn K-drama has wrapped up, but there's plenty more of Choo to watch. In the series, he plays Park Min-jae, a former swimmer who turns to robotics after losing his right leg to illness, only to find himself navigating an unexpected romance with fellow graduate student Im Yoo-jin. It's another memorable role for an actor who's been making a name for himself across different genres. From historical romances to medical dramas and crime thrillers, here are eight Choo Young-woo K-dramas worth revisiting 
 The Tale of Lady Ok (2024)
 If you loved Choo Young-woo's romantic side in Between Steps, The Tale of Lady Ok is a great place to start. Set in the Joseon era, the drama follows runaway slave Goo Deok-yi (Lim Ji-yeon), who takes on a noblewoman's identity and becomes a legal advocate defending the oppressed. Choo plays two lookalike characters: Cheon Seung-hwi, a travelling storyteller who falls for her, and Sung Yoon-gyeom, her mysterious husband. With secret identities, dangerous lies and a romance that refuses to go away, there's plenty to keep you hooked.
 Head Over Heels (2025)
 For another romance with a supernatural twist, Head Over Heels pairs Choo with Cho Yi-hyun in a story about fate and first love. Choo plays Bae Gyeon-woo, a high school student with terrible luck who's destined to die within 21 days. When Park Seong-ah (Cho Yi-hyun), a student who secretly works as a shaman, discovers his fate, she makes it her mission to save him. Of course, falling for someone whose days are numbered is never going to be easy. It's a sweet, emotional romance that brings out Choo's softer side.
 The Trauma Code: Heroes on Call (2025)
 Want to see Choo in something completely different? The Trauma Code: Heroes on Call swaps romance for medical emergencies, with Ju Ji-hoon playing Baek Kang-hyuk, a brilliant but unconventional surgeon determined to turn an underfunded trauma unit around. Choo plays Yang Jae-won, an anxious young doctor who becomes his first recruit and quickly finds himself dealing with one life-or-death emergency after another. Between the chaotic hospital shifts and his demanding mentor, Jae-won has plenty to handle. Choo's comedic timing and chemistry with Ju make their scenes especially fun to watch.

 Once Upon a Small Town (2022)
 If you're in the mood for something lighter, Once Upon a Small Town is a charming countryside romance that's easy to settle into. Choo plays Han Ji-yul, a Seoul veterinarian who reluctantly moves to a rural village to run his grandfather's animal clinic. There, he meets Ahn Ja-young (Red Velvet's Joy), a friendly local police officer who helps him navigate village life. As the two grow closer, a forgotten childhood connection adds another layer to their budding romance. With adorable animals, nosy neighbours and plenty of sweet moments, it's a refreshing change of pace.
 Oasis (2023)
 For those who enjoy a good love triangle, Oasis takes things back to South Korea in the turbulent 1980s and 1990s. Choo plays Choi Cheol-woong, a privileged young man whose friendship with Lee Doo-hak (Jang Dong-yoon) turns into a bitter rivalry when they both fall for Oh Jung-shin (Seol In-ah). Things get even messier when Doo-hak becomes involved in a criminal case that changes their lives. With jealousy, family secrets and political turmoil all thrown into the mix, Choo gets to play a much more conflicted character than his usual romantic leads.
 Mercy for None (2025)
 If you'd rather swap romance for something darker, Mercy for None takes Choo into the world of organised crime. The Netflix action thriller stars So Ji-sub as Nam Gi-jun, a former gangster who returns to the underworld after his younger brother is murdered, setting off a brutal search for revenge. Choo plays Lee Geum-son, an ambitious prosecutor with powerful family connections who gets caught up in the struggle between rival crime syndicates. Forget the sweet romantic lead you're used to seeing. Here, Choo gets to show a much colder, more calculating side.
 School 2021 (2021)
 Curious about Choo's earlier work? School 2021 is worth revisiting for a look at the actor before his recent breakthrough. Set in a vocational high school, the drama follows students figuring out friendships, first love and what they want to do with their lives. Choo plays Jung Young-joo, a guarded transfer student who holds a grudge against former friend Gong Ki-joon (Kim Yo-han) over a painful incident from their past. Add a fake relationship with ambitious classmate Kang Seo-young (Hwang Bo-reum-byeol), and Young-joo has more than enough teenage drama to deal with.
 You Make Me Dance (2021)
 To see where it all began, go back to You Make Me Dance , the short BL romance that marked Choo's acting debut. He plays Song Si-on, a contemporary dance student struggling to chase his dreams while dealing with financial troubles. When debt collector Jin Hong-seok (Won Hyung-hoon) comes knocking, Si-on convinces him to hold off until after an important audition. The two eventually end up living together, and what starts as an awkward arrangement slowly turns into something more. It's a sweet, intimate love story that offers an early glimpse of Choo's on-screen charm.
